chapter: Shows, scripts and the Mosby-era names
title: Writing Biddy Mason and Stagecoach Mary scripts; how Roots hurt
summary: After retiring, Spikes got permission from Mason's great-grandchildren and wrote her story nine years ago, but interest faded after Roots.

blocks.x: Okay. You can go on now. You were talking about Biddy [Mason].

I say, after I came home and retired, I read in the paper they had somethin' in there about Biddy, and all things and ever'thing, I say, "Well, gee whiz, as long as I know all that family and ever'thing,

I'm gonna write...write the story, and I sit down and wrote the story of Biddy Mason, and I got permission from great grandchildren, you know, got a letter over there, and it's okay to do anything I want with it. And then I got hold to scrap of paper...somethin' 'bout Stagecoach Mary, and I sent up to the library in Idaho, and they sent me all of this stuff, y'know, so I wrote that.
And then, I don't know, I got a lot of ideas that I could put down.
Yeah! Well, that's marvelous. So you wrote... you started "The Biddy Mason Story" in what year?
Nine years ago. Well, I think it's time we got it produced.

Well, you see, what killed me was when "Roots" came out. I was...I had two, three people's interested in it then but "Roots" come out, it was such a big hit they...it's...it's...a...people would say, "Well, you know, we can't do it after 'Roots,' see." "Roots" is...uh, people don't want nothin' just like it now, so, you know, it's just been waited a few weeks. But mine is not in..."Roots" nothin' like mine. Mine is...the main character's religious character, you know. What are you looking for?
